records.source_label: At the approaches to Puerto Cristobal
records.official_name: At the approaches to Puerto Cristobal
records.tss_identity_note: New TSS adopted MSC 93 (May 2014) per COLREG.2/Circ.65 (23 May 2014), implemented 0000 UTC 1 December 2014. Annex 2 comprises separation lines, three separation zones, entry and exit lanes and two inshore traffic zones (ref. chart BA 1400).
records.vts_relationship_basis: ACP Cristobal Signal Station controls anchorage entry/exit and harbour movements at the Atlantic entrance (N-2-2026) and must be called 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater, i.e. at about the inner end of the TSS. ACP does not designate it a VTS, and no source states it covers the TSS lanes.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: National (ACP) mandatory report in the direct approach: vessels must notify Cristobal Signal Station on VHF Ch 12 at 8 NM from the Atlantic Breakwater. The TSS inner end lies roughly 8 NM north of the breakwater (from Circ.65 coordinates, breakwater position not taken from a primary source), so the report falls at the landward end of the scheme, not along the lanes.
records.applicability_notes: Continuous Ch 12 watch required for vessels of 300 GT or over, 100 GT carrying passengers for hire, and commercial towing vessels of 8 m or more until an ACP pilot takes control (N-2-2026 s1b).
records.complexity_reason: TSS feeds directly into ACP-controlled anchorages and Canal waters with mandatory signal-station reporting.
records.open_questions: Does ACP (or Panama Maritime Authority, AMP) operate a formally designated VTS covering the Atlantic approaches? Exact breakwater position vs 8 NM point to be checked on chart. N-1-2026 not retrieved (N-1-2025 used).

records.source_label: In the Approaches to Galveston Bay
records.official_name: In the approaches to Galveston Bay Traffic Separation Scheme and precautionary areas (33 CFR 167.350)
records.tss_identity_note: Adopted MSC 48 (COLREG.2/Circ.20, 1983), implementation not before 17 Dec 1983. Codified at 33 CFR 167.350: inshore precautionary area, separation zone, inbound and outbound lanes, offshore precautionary area (29°06.4′N to 29°19.8′N, 94°20.6′W to 94°39.2′W).
records.vts_relationship_basis: 33 CFR 161.12 Table 1 gives the Houston-Galveston monitoring area as navigable waters north of 29°00′N, west of 94°20′W, south of 29°49′N, east of 95°20′W, which geographically contains every TSS point. 161.35 VTS area includes the Galveston Bay Entrance Channel and Outer Bar Channel, with reporting point 1 at LB 1C (29°18.2′N 94°37.6′W) inside the TSS inshore precautionary area. Caveat: Note 4 says some monitoring areas extend beyond navigable waters, where watch is not required, so the offshore end may lie outside mandatory coverage.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: No SOLAS V/11 or other mandatory ship reporting system found (WHALESNORTH/SOUTH are Atlantic-only per 33 CFR 169). Only ordinary VTS reporting under 33 CFR 161 Subpart B applies, which is not recorded as a separate scheme.
records.applicability_notes: VTS Houston-Galveston: Ch 11 north / Ch 12 south of Exxon Dock #1 line, Ch 5A for sailing plans (Table 1 to 161.12(c)). VTS users per 33 CFR 161.16.
records.complexity_reason: TSS within a statutory VTS monitoring area; offshore mandatory-watch limit depends on navigable waters extent.
records.open_questions: Whether the offshore precautionary area lies within US navigable waters (12 NM territorial sea), and so within mandatory VTS participation, was not calculated from a primary baseline source.

records.source_label: On the Pacific Coast of Panama
records.official_name: On the Pacific coast of Panama
records.tss_identity_note: New TSS adopted MSC 93 (COLREG.2/Circ.65, 23 May 2014), implemented 0000 UTC 1 December 2014. Grouped scheme: Part 1 Gulf of Panama, Part 2 Punta Morro de Puercos, Part 3 Off Isla Jicarita, Part 4 inshore traffic zones. A 10 kn seasonal speed restriction (1 Aug to 30 Nov, north of 8°00′N) applies in the Gulf of Panama part (ACP A-24-2026).
grouped_components: Part 4: Inshore traffic zones (eastern and western)
records.vts_relationship_basis: ACP Flamenco Signal Station coordinates Pacific anchorage entry/exit and harbour movements (N-2-2026). It is not designated a VTS and no source states coverage of the TSS. Parts 2 and 3 are far west of Canal waters.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: Applies to Part 1 approach only: vessels must notify Flamenco Signal Station on Ch 12 at 8 NM from the Pacific Sea Buoy ('about 11 Nautical Miles from Flamenco Island'), which is roughly at the northern (inner) end of the Gulf of Panama lanes (8°44.7′N to 8°46′N). Not applicable to Parts 2 and 3.
records.applicability_notes: Seasonal 10 kn whale speed restriction in both Gulf of Panama lanes (ACP A-24-2026).
records.complexity_reason: Grouped three-part scheme with inshore zones, seasonal speed restriction and ACP reporting at the Canal approach.
records.open_questions: Confirm whether AMP operates any coastal VTS covering Parts 2 and 3; confirm exact position of Pacific Sea Buoy relative to TSS northern end.

records.reporting_relationship_basis: WHALESNORTH (Cape Cod Bay, Massachusetts Bay, Great South Channel, south limit 41°00′N) and WHALESSOUTH (30°00′N to 31°27′N, shore to 80°51.6′W) do not cover this scheme on 33 CFR 169.105/169.115 coordinates. No other mandatory reporting system found.
records.complexity_reason: Single approach TSS with no VTS or reporting overlay evidenced.
records.open_questions: Any local Sector North Carolina port reporting practice not researched.

records.tss_identity_note: Precautionary area, Eastern Approach and Southern Approach with deep-water route for drafts over 12.8 m and naval aircraft carriers; last amended MSC 79 (COLREG.2/Circ.55), implemented 1 July 2005. Early listing in COLREG.2/Circ.5 (1978).
records.vts_relationship_basis: No USCG VTS is established for this area in 33 CFR 161 Subpart C / Table 1 to 161.12(c), and NAVCEN's VTS list (12 services) does not include one; neither source states it is exhaustive for all VTS types, so not recorded as Confirmed absent. Confirms the brief's hint: no USCG VTS at Chesapeake.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: WHALESNORTH (Cape Cod Bay, Massachusetts Bay, Great South Channel, south limit 41°00′N) and WHALESSOUTH (30°00′N to 31°27′N, shore to 80°51.6′W) do not cover this scheme on 33 CFR 169.105/169.115 coordinates. No other mandatory reporting system found.
records.applicability_notes: Southern Approach lanes for vessels drawing 12.8 m (42 ft) or less; DW route for deeper vessels and naval aircraft carriers (33 CFR 167.200(a)).
records.complexity_reason: Three parts with a deep-water route and draught-based lane use.
records.open_questions: None beyond confirming no local voluntary traffic information service.

Lead: the Maritime Exchange for the Delaware River and Bay (a trade association) receives vessel position/ETA information via its Cape Henlopen station, per search snippets (not fetched); it is not a USCG VTS.

No mandatory reporting found; Maritime Exchange reporting appears to be by request only (lead).
records.voluntary_reporting: Lead only: vessels in Delaware Bay are 'requested' to pass position/ETA to the Maritime Exchange (search snippet, not fetched).
records.complexity_reason: Four-part scheme; non-statutory port information service in the bay.
records.open_questions: Fetch Maritime Exchange / USCG Sector Delaware Bay pages to confirm service status.

records.source_label: Off New York
records.official_name: Off New York Traffic Separation Scheme and Precautionary Areas (33 CFR 167.150-155)
records.tss_identity_note: Circular precautionary area (7 NM radius on 40°27.50′N 73°49.90′W), Eastern approach off Nantucket, Eastern, South-eastern and Southern approaches, plus a junction precautionary area with the Boston TSS; amended MSC 48 (COLREG.2/Circ.20, 1983).
records.vts_relationship_basis: VTS New York exists (33 CFR 161.25; NAVCEN) but its area is bounded to the south by a line connecting the entrance buoys of Ambrose, Swash and Sandy Hook Channels, and its monitoring area (Table 1 to 161.12(c)) has the same seaward limit. The TSS approaches lie well seaward, so the CFR positively excludes the lanes. At most the landward edge of the 7 NM precautionary area may touch the VTS boundary (not verified).
records.reporting_relationship_basis: WHALESNORTH (Cape Cod Bay, Massachusetts Bay, Great South Channel, south limit 41°00′N) and WHALESSOUTH (30°00′N to 31°27′N, shore to 80°51.6′W) do not cover this scheme on 33 CFR 169.105/169.115 coordinates. The eastern end of the Nantucket approach (about 40°23′N to 40°37′N) is south of WHALESNORTH's 41°00′N limit. No other mandatory reporting found.
records.complexity_reason: Large multi-approach offshore scheme linked to the Boston TSS; VTS covers only the harbour it leads to.
records.open_questions: Check on chart whether the Ambrose/Sandy Hook entrance buoy line falls inside the 7 NM precautionary area.

records.source_label: In the Approaches to Narragansett Bay, Rhode Island and Buzzards Bay, Massachusetts
records.official_name: In the approaches to Narragansett Bay, RI, and Buzzards Bay, MA (33 CFR 167.100-103)
records.tss_identity_note: Two precautionary areas, Narragansett Bay approach and Buzzards Bay approach; amended MSC 48 (COLREG.2/Circ.20, 1983); CFR text last revised USCG-2010-0718 (2010).
records.vts_relationship_basis: No USCG VTS is established for this area in 33 CFR 161 Subpart C / Table 1 to 161.12(c), and NAVCEN's VTS list (12 services) does not include one; neither source states it is exhaustive for all VTS types, so not recorded as Confirmed absent. Buzzards Bay has a VMRS ('Buzzards Bay Control', Ch 11), defined in 33 CFR 161.2 as a mandatory reporting system, not a VTS.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: 33 CFR 161 VMRS Buzzards Bay covers waters east and north of the line Sakonnet Point, Buzzards Bay Entrance Light, Cuttyhunk Island. The Buzzards Bay approach separation zone ends at 41°21.80′N 71°07.10′W, about 3.5 NM south of that line (own calculation), so the VMRS applies in the waters the lane leads into, not in the TSS. Not applicable to the Narragansett approach. WHALESNORTH does not extend this far west.
records.applicability_notes: VMRS Buzzards Bay also applies to any vessel required to carry a bridge-to-bridge radiotelephone (note 5 to Table 1 to 161.12(c)). Navy torpedo-range restricted area note in 167.103.
records.complexity_reason: Two-branch scheme; mandatory VMRS at inner end of one branch; naval restricted area note.
records.open_questions: Editorial decision needed: whether approach-only VMRS applicability should count as 'Confirmed present' for this TSS.

records.source_label: In the Approaches to Boston, Massachusetts
records.official_name: In the approach to Boston, MA (33 CFR 167.75-77)
records.tss_identity_note: Two precautionary areas (Boston approach 6.17 NM radius on 42°22.71′N 70°46.97′W; junction with Off New York TSS near 40°35′N 69°00′W) and a TSS. Amended MSC 48 (COLREG.2/Circ.20), and again at MSC 82 (2006) and MSC 85 (2008) per circulars in S14 (circular numbers not captured).
grouped_components: Junction precautionary area with Off New York TSS
records.vts_relationship_basis: No USCG VTS is established for this area in 33 CFR 161 Subpart C / Table 1 to 161.12(c), and NAVCEN's VTS list (12 services) does not include one; neither source states it is exhaustive for all VTS types, so not recorded as Confirmed absent.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: WHALESNORTH (33 CFR 169.105) covers Massachusetts Bay and the Great South Channel down to 41°00′N. From the 167.76/167.77 coordinates, the Boston precautionary area and the lanes from 42°20′N down to 41°00′N lie inside the area (own geometry check); the southern part and the junction precautionary area (south of 41°00′N) are outside. Year-round system; self-propelled ships of 300 GT or more report on entry.
records.applicability_notes: WHALESNORTH: self-propelled ships of 300 GT or more, except SOLAS V/8-1(c) government ships; report once on entering the area (33 CFR 169.125, 169.130).
records.complexity_reason: Long TSS partly within an IMO mandatory ship reporting system; no VTS.
records.open_questions: Confirm IMO resolution number for WHALESNORTH/WHALESSOUTH (not cited in 33 CFR 169).

records.source_label: In the Approaches to Portland, Maine
records.official_name: In the approaches to Portland, ME (33 CFR 167.50-53)
records.tss_identity_note: Precautionary area (5.45 NM radius on 43°31.60′N 70°05.53′W), Eastern approach and Southern approach; listed in early circular COLREG.2/Circ.5 (1978); CFR text revised USCG-2010-0718.
records.vts_relationship_basis: No USCG VTS is established for this area in 33 CFR 161 Subpart C / Table 1 to 161.12(c), and NAVCEN's VTS list (12 services) does not include one; neither source states it is exhaustive for all VTS types, so not recorded as Confirmed absent.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: Portland TSS lies at about 43°07′N to 43°32′N, north of WHALESNORTH's northern boundary (42°39′N to 42°45′N), so WHALESNORTH does not apply. No other mandatory reporting found.
records.complexity_reason: Small port approach scheme; no overlay evidenced.
records.open_questions: None.

records.source_label: In the Bay of Fundy and approaches
records.official_name: In the Bay of Fundy and Approaches
records.tss_identity_note: Listed by CCG NOTMAR as a compulsory Canadian routeing system adopted by IMO (ref. charts 4010, 4011, 4012, 4116). Original scheme adopted early 1980s (not effective before 1 June 1983); amended MSC 76 (COLREG.2/Circ.52, 6 Jan 2003), implemented 0000 UTC 1 July 2003; amended scheme has two parts.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Bay of Fundy Local Eastern VTS Zone (SOR/2025-275 Sch. 3 item 7). RAMN Part 3 calling-in points for 'Fundy Traffic' include 'Southwest entrance to traffic separation scheme' (1A/1B), entrance/exit (4E) and north exit/entrance (5A/5B), so the TSS lies within the zone.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: SOR/2025-275 Part 4 (Local Eastern VTS Zones): sailing plan 24 h before entry from outside Canadian waters, sailing plan 15 min before entry, position reports at calling-in points, final and deviation reports. National mandatory reporting (successor to ECAREG/SOR/89-99), not IMO-adopted.
records.applicability_notes: Applies to vessels of 300 GT or more, tow/push combinations of 500 GT or more, and vessels carrying pollutants or dangerous goods; Part 4 reports also apply to vessels of 20 m or more (excluding pleasure craft under 30 m and small fishing vessels) and certain tows. Canadian modification to COLREG Rule 10 requires power-driven vessels over 20 m to use the scheme.
records.complexity_reason: Two-part compulsory scheme inside a three-sector VTS zone with statutory reporting.
records.open_questions: Part of the approach near the Canada/US boundary: confirm whether any TSS portion lies in US waters outside the zone.

records.source_label: In the Approaches to Chedabucto Bay
records.official_name: In the Approaches to Chedabucto Bay
records.tss_identity_note: Listed by CCG NOTMAR as a compulsory Canadian routeing system adopted by IMO (ref. charts 4013, 4233, 4301, 4321, 4335, 4374). Amended MSC 83 (COLREG.2/Circ.59), implemented 0000 UTC 1 May 2008; three parts.
records.vts_relationship_basis: Strait of Canso and Eastern Approaches Local Eastern VTS Zone (SOR/2025-275 Sch. 3 item 5), bounded seaward by the territorial sea limit. RAMN Table 3-24 'Canso Traffic' calling-in points include 'Entrance to inbound traffic lane' (1A, 1C), 'Exit from outbound traffic lane' (1B, 1D, 1E) and lane points 2A/2B, 3A/3B, so the TSS is within or at the zone boundary.
records.reporting_relationship_basis: SOR/2025-275 Part 4 Local Eastern VTS Zone reporting (24 h pre-entry sailing plan from outside Canadian waters, 15 min pre-entry sailing plan, calling-in-point position reports, final reports). National mandatory, not IMO-adopted.
records.applicability_notes: As for Bay of Fundy (SOR/2025-275 ss 3 and 24). Parts of the TSS seaward of the territorial sea limit may fall within the Eastern VTS Zone (Schedule 2) instead.
records.complexity_reason: Compulsory scheme at the edge of a local VTS zone; zone boundary follows the territorial sea limit through the lanes.
records.open_questions: Exact split of the TSS between the Local Zone and the Eastern VTS Zone at the territorial sea limit.

method_notes: eCFR API (versioner full XML, needs Accept-Encoding compression) gave complete 33 CFR 161, 167 and 169 texts in three calls and was the best US source. For geography checks, TSS coordinates were compared with VTS/reporting boundaries by hand calculation (flagged as own analysis). Canada: the Vessel Traffic Services Zones Regulations SOR/2025-275 came into force 31 March 2026 and repealed SOR/89-98 and SOR/89-99 (ECAREG), so older ECAREG references should be updated. The RAMN 2026 PDF (10 MB) would not download (HTTP/2 stream errors), but the HTML Part 2 and Part 3 pages worked and give calling-in points naming the TSS. IMO adoption data came from a Swedish Transport Agency compilation of COLREG.2 circulars (OCR text without spaces in older circulars); COLREG.2/Circ.65 from the Panama ship registry site. Panama Canal Authority notices (N-1, N-2, advisories) downloaded well as PDFs. Access problems: no Cuban official source found; Mexican hacienda.gob.mx PDFs returned 503 or failed TLS verification; SEMAR/APIVER VTS pages not found. Suggest adding IMO Ships' Routeing current edition or NGA Pub. 140/148 sailing directions for Cuba and Mexico, and deciding editorially whether reporting that applies only in a TSS's direct approach counts as 'Confirmed present'.
